subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should native OpenAI use the existing cache-ttl pruning semantics, or should this issue wait for a provider-agnostic pruning mode?
rationale: Current source proves the configured path is gated off, but enabling OpenAI changes existing session-retention behavior and prior PR review identified TTL semantics as a maintainer choice.

options.title: Approve native OpenAI cache-ttl semantics
options.body: Keep the open PR direction, require native idle-gap proof, and make the OpenAI TTL/session policy explicit before merge.

options.title: Design provider-agnostic pruning first
options.body: Leave OpenAI cache eligibility unchanged and solve the report with a new pruning mode that is not tied to prompt-cache eligibility.

options.title: Defer to broader cache work
options.body: Keep this issue open as dependent on broader OpenAI prefix-cache fixes such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95610.

recommendation.title: Approve native OpenAI cache-ttl semantics
recommendation.body: Keep the open PR direction, require native idle-gap proof, and make the OpenAI TTL/session policy explicit before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current helper/gate blame and recent cache-TTL history point to this owner candidate for the immediate policy and implementation decision.
